name: Patina Green
lede: Patina Green is a deep, slightly blue-leaning green named for the oxidized coating that forms on copper and bronze, and it is also RAL 6000, a 1927 German industrial color standard.

sections.title: A patina, standardized
sections.body:
Patina is the thin, naturally formed surface layer, often green, that copper and bronze develop as they weather [1]. RAL set its version as RAL 6000, Patina Green, one of its earliest industrial color standards, founded in Germany in 1927 [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS system lists the same area as block 135, "light yellowish green," about 2.4 units from this exact shade [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[deep-jade]], [[light-danube-green]], [[tropical-rainforest]] and [[blue-green]], at 3, 3.3, 3.5 and 4.2 ΔE [1]. The closest name in the Maerz and Paul dictionary dates to about 1894, three decades before RAL's standard [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
In our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, this green appears in only 40, about 0.17 percent, rarer than 64 percent of our named colors [2]. It peaks in the 1800s, in 11 of 8,345 paintings, at 1.8 times the expected rate for that century, and it is most over-represented in paintings from France, at 2.7 times the expected rate [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a mid-tone rather than a light or a shadow [2].

The earliest match is a 1728 still life by [[painter:jan-van-huysum|Jan van Huysum]], about two centuries before RAL's 1927 standard, so that early hit is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph and not evidence of any real patina on the canvas, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].

questions.q: True or false: Patina Green is the only name our library files in ISCC-NBS block 135.

openers: ISCC-NBS block 135 is crowded enough to hold Patina Green alongside Egyptian Green, Lizard Green and Spruce Green.
Patina Green is RAL's standardized version of the real green crust that forms on weathered copper.
